title: Supporting Large Capital Delivery
narrative: We require a project and programme management capability in the architecture, represented in the business and application domains. This is based on a requirement for the business to support Large Capital Project delivery going forward, enabling delivery both internally and through external vendors and suppliers. The capability and its supporting application must interface with the existing ERP and CRM platforms so that project, financial, and customer data flow coherently across the enterprise.

referential-integrity.finding: All parent-id references in BUS-CAP are internally consistent. Every level-2 capability references a defined level-1 parent (CAP-001 through CAP-009), and every level-3 capability references a defined level-2 parent (CAP-001-01, CAP-002-02, CAP-003-02, CAP-004-04, CAP-006-03). No dangling parent-id values exist in architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json.
referential-integrity.impact: The existing BUS-CAP catalogue is internally coherent. No remediation is required for the current state. The proposed addition of CAP-010 and its level-2 sub-capabilities (as recommended by the architecture review) will introduce new IDs; those new entries must themselves carry no unresolvable parent-id values when authored.
referential-integrity.recommendation: When adding CAP-010 and its level-2 sub-capabilities to BUS-CAP, ensure each level-2 entry carries parent-id set to CAP-010, and that no level-3 entries are added without a corresponding level-2 parent already present in the same commit.
referential-integrity.rationale: The BUS-CAP schema requires parent-id to reference an existing capability ID. Authoring parent and child entries atomically in a single commit prevents a window where a dangling parent-id could be introduced and not caught until validation runs.

referential-integrity.finding: All domain-id references in APP-DAP are internally consistent. Every platform entry in architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/application/logical/APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json references one of the eleven domain IDs defined in the domains array of the same file (APP-DOM-CUSTOMER, APP-DOM-FIELD, APP-DOM-TRADING, APP-DOM-NETWORK, APP-DOM-BILLING, APP-DOM-METERING, APP-DOM-REGULATORY, APP-DOM-SUSTAIN, APP-DOM-DATA, APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE, APP-DOM-INTEGRATION). No duplicate platform or domain IDs exist.
referential-integrity.impact: The existing APP-DAP catalogue is internally coherent. The proposed addition of PLAT-PPM (as recommended by the architecture review) will reference APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE; that domain ID is already defined, so the new platform entry will resolve correctly without any additional domain-level change.
referential-integrity.recommendation: When adding PLAT-PPM to APP-DAP, set its domain-id to APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE. No new domain entry is needed. Verify no other new platform IDs clash with existing PLAT-* identifiers in the same file before committing.
referential-integrity.rationale: APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE already covers corporate services including the ERP platform; PPM is a natural extension of that domain boundary. Reusing an existing domain ID avoids introducing an unvalidated new domain and keeps the catalogue consistent with the current domain taxonomy.

referential-integrity.finding: BUS-PRO at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json contains an empty processes array. There are no cross-catalogue references from BUS-PRO to BUS-CAP capability IDs in the current schema or instance, so no dangling references exist. However, the BUS-PRO schema does not currently define a capability-id or parent-capability-id link field, making forward traceability from processes to capabilities impossible to validate structurally.
referential-integrity.impact: Once processes are added to BUS-PRO (as recommended by the architecture review following the addition of CAP-010), there is no schema-enforced foreign key from a process to its owning capability. Referential integrity between BUS-PRO and BUS-CAP cannot be automatically checked with the current schema definition.
referential-integrity.recommendation: When authoring new process entries in BUS-PRO, include a convention-based capability-id field referencing the relevant CAP-NNN identifier from BUS-CAP, even if the field is not yet schema-enforced. Note the absence of schema-level cross-catalogue validation as a gap to be addressed in a future schema update to BUS-PRO.
referential-integrity.rationale: Establishing the capability-to-process link by convention now, even without schema enforcement, provides a traceable record that can be mechanically validated once the BUS-PRO schema is updated. Waiting until the schema is updated before adding the field would leave the traceability gap unresolvable in retrospect.

strategy-alignment.finding: BUS-STR-002 (architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-STR/BUS-STR.json) states that all value-creating work will be delivered by persistent product teams by 2026 and explicitly excludes project-based funding for in-life products. The proposed ADR introduces a Project and Programme Management capability (CAP-010) structured around capital project lifecycle, programme governance, and vendor-managed delivery — a delivery model that is definitionally project-based rather than product-team-based.
strategy-alignment.impact: The proposed capability is in direct tension with BUS-STR-002. If adopted without qualification, CAP-010 could be interpreted as endorsing project-based delivery as a general operating model, which contradicts the documented strategic direction. This tension will surface in any future strategy-to-capability traceability review.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Scope CAP-010 explicitly to large capital infrastructure or asset investment programmes — contexts where discrete, bounded project delivery is structurally unavoidable — and add a description to the capability entry that distinguishes it from the product-team delivery model mandated by BUS-STR-002. Consider adding a note in the BUS-PRO processes for this capability that references BUS-STR-002 as an explicit boundary condition.
strategy-alignment.rationale: BUS-STR-002 is not silent on project delivery — it actively excludes it for in-life products. Scoping CAP-010 to capital investment programmes creates a defensible, documented exception rather than an undifferentiated contradiction. This prevents the capability from being read as a strategic reversal and keeps the architecture coherent.

strategy-alignment.finding: BUS-STR-004 (BUS-STR.json) requires that investment follows learning and that no business case lifecycle exceeds the time to first learning. Large capital delivery programmes are characterised by long planning horizons, fixed-scope commitments, and high change-control overhead — a pattern that is structurally at odds with the quarterly rebalancing and continuous discovery outcome targeted by BUS-STR-004.
strategy-alignment.impact: Introducing a PPM capability without acknowledging BUS-STR-004 risks embedding a delivery model that conflicts with the organisation's stated investment governance strategy. Future architecture reviews may flag the capability as undermining BUS-STR-004 unless the tension is surfaced and resolved.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Document in the ADR narrative or the BUS-PRO process entries for CAP-010 that large capital programmes are treated as a bounded exception to the BUS-STR-004 continuous-discovery model, and that the PPM capability should incorporate stage-gated learning checkpoints (e.g. at project initiation and design completion) to partially satisfy the BUS-STR-004 intent.
strategy-alignment.rationale: Acknowledging the tension with BUS-STR-004 and prescribing a mitigation approach (learning checkpoints within a capital delivery lifecycle) demonstrates strategic awareness and reduces the likelihood of the capability being challenged or deprioritised in a future strategy review.

strategy-alignment.finding: BUS-STR-005 (BUS-STR.json) targets the top 20 business processes fully digital end-to-end by 2026. Capital project initiation, delivery controls, and vendor management are high-volume, document-heavy processes that typically rely on manual handovers and bespoke spreadsheets — exactly the pattern BUS-STR-005 seeks to eliminate. The proposed PPM capability, if implemented with a fit-for-purpose digital platform, directly advances this strategic outcome.
strategy-alignment.impact: The proposed change is aligned with BUS-STR-005. A well-scoped PPM capability with supporting PLAT-PPM tooling provides a mechanism to digitise capital project processes and contributes to the BUS-STR-005 target. This alignment strengthens the case for the ADR.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: Reference BUS-STR-005 explicitly when describing the PPM platform (PLAT-PPM) in APP-DAP. Include process digitisation — replacing manual project controls and spreadsheet-based reporting — as a stated objective of the PLAT-PPM entry to make the alignment traceable.
strategy-alignment.rationale: Making the BUS-STR-005 alignment explicit in the APP-DAP platform description creates a traceable justification for the platform investment and supports any future capability-to-strategy review.

strategy-alignment.finding: APP-STR-002 (architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/application/conceptual/APP-STR/APP-STR.json) mandates buying or assembling commodity capability rather than building it, with custom build reserved for differentiating capabilities. Project and programme management tooling is a well-established commodity software category. The architecture review recommendation to add PLAT-PPM to APP-DAP is consistent with APP-STR-002, provided the platform is sourced as a commercial or SaaS product rather than custom-built.
strategy-alignment.impact: The proposed direction is aligned with APP-STR-002. No conflict exists, but the lifecycle value assigned to PLAT-PPM (trial or adopt as recommended by the architecture review) should be backed by a vendor or product selection decision to remain consistent with the buy-or-assemble intent.
strategy-alignment.recommendation: When authoring the PLAT-PPM entry in APP-DAP, set the description to reference a specific commercial PPM product or product category if one has been identified, and set lifecycle to trial until a product selection is confirmed. Avoid any language that implies custom development of the PPM platform.
strategy-alignment.rationale: APP-STR-002 sets a clear expectation that commodity capability is sourced, not built. Anchoring the PLAT-PPM entry to a commercial product selection keeps the application architecture consistent with this strategy and avoids inadvertently implying a custom-build path.

principles-alignment.finding: BUS-PRN-001 requires capabilities to reflect what the business does, independent of organisational structure, with process and application investments mapped to capabilities first. The proposed addition of CAP-010 Project and Programme Management to BUS-CAP is consistent with this principle: the capability is defined by the outcome (delivering large capital projects) rather than by a named team or division. The recommended additions to BUS-PRO and APP-DAP are both anchored to CAP-010 as their capability root.
principles-alignment.impact: The change adheres to BUS-PRN-001. No remediation is required, but the principle reinforces the architecture-review recommendation that BUS-CAP must be updated before BUS-PRO or APP-DAP entries are authored, to preserve the capability-first investment mapping sequence.
principles-alignment.recommendation: Proceed with the capability-first sequencing already recommended by the architecture review: add CAP-010 to BUS-CAP before authoring BUS-PRO process entries or the PLAT-PPM entry in APP-DAP. Document the capability-to-process and capability-to-platform links explicitly in each artefact.
principles-alignment.rationale: BUS-PRN-001 explicitly states that process and application investments are mapped to capabilities first. Authoring the dependent artefacts before the capability anchor is present would violate this principle and undermine traceability.

principles-alignment.finding: BUS-PRN-004 (Continuous discovery over big design up front) states that no initiative passes commitment without an evidence-based shaping phase, and that funding is staged against learning milestones, not Gantt milestones. Large capital delivery programmes are structurally characterised by long planning horizons and fixed-scope commitments. The proposed CAP-010 and its sub-capabilities (programme governance, capital project delivery, project controls) describe a delivery model that is in tension with BUS-PRN-004 unless the capability is explicitly scoped to bounded infrastructure investment where stage-gated learning is structurally incorporated.
principles-alignment.impact: Without explicit qualification, CAP-010 and the supporting BUS-PRO processes risk being interpreted as endorsing big-design-up-front delivery as a general operating model, which directly contradicts BUS-PRN-004. This tension will surface in any future principles-compliance review.
principles-alignment.recommendation: Scope CAP-010's description to large capital infrastructure or asset investment programmes where discrete project delivery is unavoidable, and ensure the BUS-PRO process entries for capital project initiation and delivery include stage-gated learning checkpoints as an explicit process step. Reference BUS-PRN-004 as a boundary condition in the ADR narrative.
principles-alignment.rationale: BUS-PRN-004 is not silent on long-horizon delivery — it actively requires evidence-based staging. Documenting a scoped exception and a mitigation mechanism (learning checkpoints) creates a defensible, traceable compliance position rather than an undifferentiated violation.

principles-alignment.finding: BUS-PRN-006 (Process digital by default) requires that new or redesigned business processes are fully digital end-to-end unless a documented constraint requires manual steps, and that process designs ship with a data model and event flow. Capital project delivery and vendor management processes are historically document-heavy and manual-handover-intensive. The proposed change introduces these processes into the architecture but does not yet address their digital execution design.
principles-alignment.impact: If BUS-PRO process entries for CAP-010 are authored without committing to digital execution, they will be non-compliant with BUS-PRN-006 from the moment they are created. The architecture review already identifies PLAT-PPM as the application platform to support these processes, which provides a foundation for digital execution, but the link must be made explicit.
principles-alignment.recommendation: When authoring BUS-PRO entries for CAP-010 processes, include a statement that each process is to be executed fully digitally via PLAT-PPM (or a named successor), and identify any manual steps that require a documented constraint justification. Set PLAT-PPM's lifecycle value to trial or adopt (not retire or tolerate) to signal active digital investment.
principles-alignment.rationale: BUS-PRN-006 requires the digital commitment to be made at process design time, not retrofitted later. Tying the BUS-PRO entries to PLAT-PPM at authoring time satisfies the principle and creates a traceable link between the process catalogue and the application platform.

principles-alignment.finding: APP-PRN-002 (Composable over monolithic) requires that new capabilities are published via stable, versioned interfaces and are independently replaceable. The proposed PLAT-PPM entry will be a commercial or SaaS PPM product (consistent with APP-STR-002 as assessed in strategy-alignment). Commercial PPM tools vary significantly in how well they expose integration interfaces: some provide mature APIs, others are closed ecosystems. The APP-DAP catalogue does not yet include interface or integration posture metadata, so compliance with APP-PRN-002 cannot be fully assessed at this stage.
principles-alignment.impact: If PLAT-PPM is sourced as a closed-ecosystem tool with limited integration interfaces, the application architecture will have a platform that is de facto non-replaceable and cannot compose with other platforms (e.g. PLAT-ERP for project accounting) without custom integration work. This would violate APP-PRN-002.
principles-alignment.recommendation: When selecting the PPM product and authoring the PLAT-PPM entry in APP-DAP, include in the description whether the product exposes a versioned API for data exchange, and note any known integration constraints. Treat the availability of stable, versioned integration interfaces as a non-functional requirement in the product selection decision.
principles-alignment.rationale: APP-PRN-002 makes replaceability a first-class design quality assessed at architecture review. Recording the integration posture at the time the platform entry is authored ensures this quality can be evaluated now rather than discovered as a constraint when an integration or replacement is needed.

proponent-analysis.finding: All four upstream analysis sections confirm that the proposed change is architecturally additive: no existing artefact needs to be removed or restructured, only new entries added to BUS-CAP, BUS-PRO, and APP-DAP. The referential-integrity check found no violations in the current catalogues, and the architecture-review confirms that all three target artefact types are already schema-backed and in scope for instance-level changes.
proponent-analysis.impact: The path to implementation is low-friction. There are no blocking defects in the existing catalogues, no new artefact types to define, no schema authoring required, and no folder structure changes needed. The change can be executed entirely through instance file edits in three existing files.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Proceed with authoring the three instance file changes identified by the architecture-review: add CAP-010 to BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json, add process entries to BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json, and add PLAT-PPM to APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json. No other files need to change to implement the core of this ADR.
proponent-analysis.rationale: When upstream checks confirm clean referential integrity and a clear, bounded set of file changes using existing schemas, the risk profile for proceeding is low. Deferring a well-scoped, non-breaking addition does not reduce risk; it only delays the traceability benefits the change provides.

proponent-analysis.finding: The strategy-alignment section identified positive alignment between the proposed PLAT-PPM application platform and both BUS-STR-005 (top 20 processes digital end-to-end by 2026) and APP-STR-002 (buy or assemble commodity capability). Capital project processes are explicitly the kind of manual, document-heavy workflows BUS-STR-005 targets, and PPM tooling is a mature commodity software category consistent with APP-STR-002.
proponent-analysis.impact: The change simultaneously advances two documented strategic outcomes: process digitisation and commodity sourcing. This dual alignment strengthens the business case for the ADR and reduces the likelihood of it being challenged in a future strategy or investment review.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Make the BUS-STR-005 and APP-STR-002 alignments explicit in the PLAT-PPM entry description in APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json. Reference process digitisation as a stated objective and anchor the platform to a commercial product category to satisfy the buy-or-assemble intent.
proponent-analysis.rationale: Traceable strategy alignment in the artefact data itself — not only in the ADR narrative — means the alignment is discoverable in any future capability-to-strategy or platform-to-strategy query against the architecture model, providing durable justification for the investment.

proponent-analysis.finding: The principles-alignment section confirmed that BUS-PRN-001 (capability-first investment mapping) actively supports the sequencing already recommended by the architecture-review: BUS-CAP must be updated before BUS-PRO or APP-DAP are authored. BUS-PRN-006 (process digital by default) and APP-PRN-002 (composable over monolithic) both have clear, actionable compliance paths that can be satisfied within this ADR by including digital execution statements in BUS-PRO entries and integration posture metadata in the PLAT-PPM description.
proponent-analysis.impact: The principles provide a ready-made compliance checklist for the authoring work. Meeting BUS-PRN-001, BUS-PRN-006, and APP-PRN-002 within this ADR produces a set of artefacts that will pass a principles-compliance review without requiring follow-up remediation work.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Use the sequencing and content guidance from the principles-alignment findings as an authoring checklist: (1) add CAP-010 first, (2) include digital execution statements in each BUS-PRO process entry referencing PLAT-PPM, (3) include integration posture metadata in the PLAT-PPM APP-DAP entry. This satisfies BUS-PRN-001, BUS-PRN-006, and APP-PRN-002 in a single authoring pass.
proponent-analysis.rationale: Principles compliance is easier and cheaper to build in at authoring time than to retrofit. The upstream analysis has already identified exactly what metadata is needed; including it now avoids a future remediation ADR and keeps the architecture coherent from the first version of these artefacts.

proponent-analysis.finding: The strategy-alignment section identified two tensions — with BUS-STR-002 (product teams over project delivery) and BUS-STR-004 (continuous discovery over big design up front) — but both are resolvable by explicit scoping rather than by withdrawing the proposed change. The proposed capability is only in conflict if it is read as endorsing project-based delivery as a general model; scoped to large capital infrastructure investment, it is a necessary and documented exception.
proponent-analysis.impact: The tensions with BUS-STR-002 and BUS-STR-004 do not invalidate the ADR. They are boundary conditions that, once documented in the capability and process descriptions, convert the apparent contradictions into traceable, defensible exceptions. The change remains justified; it requires qualification, not rejection.
proponent-analysis.recommendation: Add explicit scoping language to the CAP-010 description in BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json that restricts the capability to large capital infrastructure or asset investment programmes. Add stage-gated learning checkpoints as an explicit step in the BUS-PRO process entries for capital project initiation and delivery. Reference BUS-STR-002 and BUS-PRN-004 as boundary conditions in the ADR narrative.
proponent-analysis.rationale: Documenting exceptions with their rationale and boundary conditions is architecturally sound practice. The alternative — leaving the scoping implicit — creates ambiguity that will be raised in every future review. A single, explicit qualification now eliminates a recurring objection and makes the architecture self-documenting on this point.

challenger-analysis.finding: BUS-STR-002 explicitly excludes project-based funding for in-life products, targeting persistent product teams as the delivery model by 2026. BUS-PRN-004 further requires that no initiative passes commitment without an evidence-based shaping phase and that funding is staged against learning milestones, not Gantt milestones. The proposed CAP-010 and its sub-capabilities (programme governance, capital project delivery, project controls) describe a delivery model structurally characterised by fixed-scope commitments and long planning horizons. Neither BUS-STR-002 nor BUS-PRN-004 contains a documented exception clause for capital infrastructure programmes at this time.
challenger-analysis.impact: Adopting CAP-010 without a formally documented and agreed exception risks establishing a precedent that project-based delivery is an acceptable general operating model, directly contradicting BUS-STR-002 and BUS-PRN-004. Every future initiative seeking to avoid the product-team model may cite CAP-010 as justification, progressively eroding the strategic and principles-level constraints the organisation has documented.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Before proceeding, obtain explicit sign-off from the accountable strategy owner that large capital infrastructure delivery constitutes a recognised exception to BUS-STR-002 and BUS-PRN-004, and record that exception in the relevant BUS-STR and BUS-PRN instance files — not only in the ADR narrative. Authoring the exception only in transient ADR text leaves the catalogues internally inconsistent.
challenger-analysis.rationale: The architecture catalogues are the authoritative state; the ADR is a change record, not a persistent constraint register. If the exception is not recorded in BUS-STR and BUS-PRN, future queries against those catalogues will surface an unqualified conflict with CAP-010 indefinitely, creating ongoing confusion and rework.

challenger-analysis.finding: The architecture-review recommends adding PLAT-PPM to APP-DAP with lifecycle set to trial if no tool has been selected, or adopt if one is in use. The referential-integrity and principles-alignment checks note that APP-PRN-002 (composable over monolithic) requires stable, versioned integration interfaces, and that the APP-DAP schema contains no integration posture metadata field to enforce this. As of the current catalogues, no PPM product has been identified, evaluated, or selected. A lifecycle value of trial without a named product is semantically vacuous — it records intent without commitment.
challenger-analysis.impact: Adding PLAT-PPM as an unanchored placeholder expands the application catalogue with an entry that cannot be validated against APP-STR-002 (buy or assemble) or APP-PRN-002 (composable interfaces) until a product is named. Future architecture queries will return PLAT-PPM as a platform in scope, potentially influencing integration design decisions, without any evidence that a compliant product exists.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Defer the addition of PLAT-PPM to APP-DAP until a candidate product or product category has been identified through a formal shaping or discovery exercise. If the ADR must proceed now, add PLAT-PPM with an explicit placeholder note in the description field stating that no product has been selected, and set lifecycle to trial with a clear expectation that a follow-up ADR will name a specific product and confirm APP-PRN-002 compliance.
challenger-analysis.rationale: An application catalogue entry that cannot be evaluated against the organisation's own application strategy and principles principles is an architectural liability, not an asset. Deferring or explicitly qualifying the entry prevents it from being mistaken for a confirmed architectural decision.

challenger-analysis.finding: The BUS-PRO catalogue is currently empty. The architecture-review identifies a need for at least three new process entries aligned to CAP-010, and the principles-alignment section flags that BUS-PRN-006 requires each process to be authored with a commitment to digital execution and an identified data model and event flow. The current BUS-PRO schema does not enforce a data-model or event-flow field, and there is no cross-catalogue validation between BUS-PRO and BUS-CAP. The proponent-analysis characterises this as low-friction, but the absence of schema enforcement means BUS-PRO entries can be authored without meeting BUS-PRN-006 with no automated check to detect the gap.
challenger-analysis.impact: If BUS-PRO entries for CAP-010 are authored now, at a time when PLAT-PPM has no confirmed product, they will reference a digital execution platform that does not yet exist. Process entries committed against an unconfirmed platform create a false picture of digital readiness and may be used to justify downstream integration or solution-layer work that is premature.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Sequence BUS-PRO authoring after PLAT-PPM is anchored to a specific product. If both are authored in this ADR, ensure the BUS-PRO entries carry an explicit caveat that digital execution is conditional on PLAT-PPM product selection, and raise a schema gap issue for BUS-PRO to enforce the data-model and event-flow fields required by BUS-PRN-006.
challenger-analysis.rationale: Process entries that reference an unconfirmed platform introduce a dependency that is invisible to schema validation. Recording the conditionality explicitly in the process descriptions and raising the schema gap ensures the architecture remains honest about what is decided versus what is aspirational.

challenger-analysis.finding: The proponent-analysis concludes that the change is low-risk because it is additive and uses existing schemas, and recommends proceeding immediately with three instance file edits. However, the strategy-alignment section identifies two unresolved tensions (BUS-STR-002, BUS-STR-004) and the principles-alignment section identifies two compliance risks (BUS-PRN-004, APP-PRN-002) that are characterised as resolvable by scoping language alone. In all four cases, the upstream analysis recommends adding qualifying language to descriptions and process entries — a soft control that is neither schema-enforced nor validated by any existing workflow.
challenger-analysis.impact: The combined weight of two strategy tensions and two principles compliance risks, all mitigated only by unvalidated free-text qualifications, represents a higher cumulative risk than the proponent-analysis acknowledges. If any of the qualifying language is omitted, misworded, or interpreted differently by a later reviewer, the architecture will contain entries that are non-compliant with documented strategy and principles with no automated detection.
challenger-analysis.recommendation: Do not treat free-text scoping language as a sufficient control for strategy and principles compliance. Before marking this ADR as approved, define and apply at least one structural control — for example, a required description field pattern, a CI validation rule, or a linked constraint record in BUS-STR or BUS-PRN — that makes the exception machine-detectable. If no such control can be put in place within this ADR, defer approval until the control is defined.
challenger-analysis.rationale: Architecture governance that relies entirely on authoring discipline for compliance is fragile. The value of the Architecture as Code model is that structural constraints can be validated automatically. Accepting soft controls as the sole mitigation for documented strategy and principles tensions undermines the governance model this repository is designed to support.

impact-assessment.finding: The BUS-CAP catalogue at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json defines nine level-1 capabilities (CAP-001 through CAP-009). None represents Project and Programme Management. CAP-005 (Asset Management) includes CAP-005-02 Acquire and Construct Assets, which touches capital delivery only incidentally, and CAP-009 (Enterprise Support) covers corporate services generically. Neither provides an anchor for programme governance, capital project lifecycle, or vendor-managed delivery.
impact-assessment.impact: The narrative explicitly requires a project and programme management capability in the business domain. Without a dedicated level-1 entry in BUS-CAP, no downstream artefact — BUS-PRO processes, BUS-PRN principles, or APP-DAP platform mappings — can be correctly traced to a declared business capability. Any future strategy-alignment or capability-to-application mapping check will fail for this change.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Add a new level-1 capability CAP-010 Project and Programme Management to architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json with importance set to strategic. Add at least three level-2 sub-capabilities under it: CAP-010-01 Portfolio and Programme Governance, CAP-010-02 Capital Project Delivery, and CAP-010-03 Project Controls and Reporting. CAP-010-02 should explicitly reference both internal and vendor/supplier delivery modes to reflect the narrative requirement.
impact-assessment.rationale: BUS-CAP is the authoritative business capability register for this client version. Registering a new top-level capability before any dependent artefacts are authored ensures that all downstream work in the business, application, and data domains can be coherently traced back to a single, versioned anchor.

impact-assessment.finding: The APP-DAP catalogue at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/application/logical/APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json contains no platform for end-to-end project or programme management. PLAT-ERP (APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE) covers finance, procurement, and project accounting but does not represent a PPM or project scheduling tool. No other platform in the catalogue addresses project planning, resource management, programme governance, or vendor/contractor coordination.
impact-assessment.impact: Without a PPM platform entry in APP-DAP, the application layer has no support for the capability being introduced in BUS-CAP. The proposed change requires the business to deliver large capital projects both internally and through external vendors; neither delivery mode is reflected in the current application catalogue. Capability-to-application traceability cannot be established, and the application domain remains incomplete at the logical layer.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Add a new platform entry PLAT-PPM Project and Programme Management to APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json, associated with APP-DOM-ENTERPRISE (consistent with the existing enterprise support domain boundary). The description should cover project scheduling, resource and capacity management, programme governance, and integration with PLAT-ERP for project accounting and cost management. Assign a lifecycle value of trial if no tool has been adopted yet, or adopt if one is already in use.
impact-assessment.rationale: APP-DAP is the single catalogue of logical application platforms for this client version. Introducing a business capability without a corresponding application platform creates a gap at the logical layer that cannot be resolved at the physical or solution layers without first being declared here.

impact-assessment.finding: The BUS-PRO catalogue at architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json is currently empty (processes array is []). The narrative introduces a project and programme management capability that will require business processes to be defined — at minimum covering capital project initiation, delivery governance, and vendor management.
impact-assessment.impact: An empty BUS-PRO catalogue is acceptable as a starting state, but once CAP-010 is added to BUS-CAP, the absence of corresponding BUS-PRO entries will leave the conceptual business domain incomplete. Process-level analysis and capability-to-process mapping will not be possible until processes are defined.
impact-assessment.recommendation: After adding CAP-010 to BUS-CAP, add at least three process entries to BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json aligned to the new capability: capital project initiation and approval, capital project delivery and controls, and vendor and supplier management. This work can follow in a subsequent ADR or as part of this one.
impact-assessment.rationale: BUS-PRO and BUS-CAP are both conceptual business-domain catalogues; completeness at the conceptual layer requires both capabilities and their supporting processes to be declared. Noting the gap now ensures it is tracked and not overlooked when the application and integration domains are subsequently populated.

impact-assessment.finding: No new artefact types need to be created to represent this change. BUS-CAP, BUS-PRO, and APP-DAP are all existing, schema-backed catalogue types that cover the required content. The artefact-type registry in documentation/artefacts.md does not need modification.
impact-assessment.impact: Confining the change to instance data in existing artefact types avoids the overhead of schema authoring, schema documentation, artefact-type registry updates, and new folder creation that would be required if a new artefact type were introduced.
impact-assessment.recommendation: Proceed by updating instance files only: architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-CAP/BUS-CAP.json, architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/business/conceptual/BUS-PRO/BUS-PRO.json, and architectures/clients/client-a/1.0.0/artefacts/domains/application/logical/APP-DAP/APP-DAP.json.
impact-assessment.rationale: Reusing existing artefact types is the correct approach when the required content fits within already-defined schemas. New artefact types are only warranted when an entirely new output format or domain-layer combination is needed, which is not the case here.

history.notes: Decision raised to support large capital delivery requirements.
